analysis:
Both changed files are test-only Swift sources. No production code, coordinator contract, key handling, attestation, or authorization path is modified.

1) ModelPrefixBenchmarkFixture.swift (head lines 41-53): checkpointEnvironment now also pins EngineV2Factory.prefillChunkKey and stepTokenBudgetKey from a default CBv2SchedulerConfig() whenever a specification pins soloPrefillStripeTokens. This only affects the benchmark/qualification fixture environment, which is passed to makeBenchmarkSession as an explicit dictionary and not to the process environment. The fixture still pins DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_TEST_ROOT, uses an ephemeral or persistent test namespace, and disables the memory tier. The at-rest properties in T-041 (HMAC-keyed names, TTL, KEK) are unchanged. The change alters prefill geometry only in tests, so it has no effect on cross-tenant sharing or the TTFT oracle (SEC-035).

2) LaunchAgentRestartTests.swift (head lines 181-204): the new test asserts that the prefill-chunk and step-token-budget rollback variables pass through LaunchAgent.passthroughEnvironment into the plist. It also asserts that UNRELATED_SECRET is excluded and that WatchdogAgent does not forward these keys. This confirms the allowlist rejects arbitrary variables. The test depends on the production allowlist (LaunchAgent.inferencePassthroughEnvKeys) already containing these keys. That allowlist is not in this batch, so whether production forwards the keys is unverified. If this PR also changes the allowlist, it needs separate review. The forwarded values are numeric tuning knobs set by the operator, who is already trusted for local configuration. They give no new privilege beyond what TB-003 already assumes.

No security regression was identified. The remaining open question is whether the production allowlist and EngineV2Factory.prefillGeometry changes elsewhere in the PR handle malformed values safely.
